speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, such as whether it is raised, flat, or blistering? Also, did the rash appear before or after the fever and other symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a prodromal illness followed by a facial rash sparing the perioral area and then spreading to the trunk and extremities is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease, caused by Parvovirus B19. Do you have any joint pain or swelling, and has anyone else in her household or school had a similar "slapped cheek" rash recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19, given the prodrome followed by a facial rash sparing the perioral area and subsequent spread. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
